Adoption Notice of CCSDS 131.0-B-5, TM Synchronization and Channel Coding
short_title: ECSS Adoption Notice of CCSDS 131.0-B-5 (TM coding)
organisation: ECSS Secretariat, ESA-ESTEC Requirements & Standards Section (prepared by the ECSS Space Communications Working Group)
status_notes: ECSS-E-AS-50-21C Rev. 2 of 5 December 2024 is 'First issue, Revision 2'. It follows ECSS-E-AS-50-21C (1 March 2021, first issue, which superseded ECSS-E-ST-50-01C of 31 July 2008) and ECSS-E-AS-50-21C Rev.1 (13 January 2023) (change log, p. 3). The context clause states that ECSS-E-ST-50-01C is superseded by ECSS-E-AS-50-21 (latest version) (p. 6). Whether a later revision exists is not stated in the document.

key_points.text: Requirement ECSS-E-AS-50-21_1520001 makes CCSDS 131.0-B-5, TM Synchronization and Channel Coding, Issue 5 (September 2023) applicable as written with the amendments of Table 4-1.

Rev. 2 updates the notice to the CCSDS issue that adds a revised pseudo-randomizer for high-data-rate links, and adds previously missed differences concerning USLP, turbo code rates and ASM bit patterns; Rev.1 (13 January 2023) had added USLP and ground-to-space support.

Mapping of superseded standards: ECSS-E-ST-50-01C maps to ECSS-E-AS-50-21 (CCSDS 131.0-B-x); ECSS-E-ST-50-03C to -22 (132.0-B-x) and -23 (732.0-B-x); ECSS-E-ST-50-04C to -24 (231.0-B-x), -25 (232.0-B-x) and -26 (232.1-B-x).
Clause 3.2.4 is modified: soft bit decisions with at least three-bit quantization shall be used for the decoder of the convolutional code (CCSDS says 'should ... whenever constraints permit').
New requirement 4.3.1c: the Reed-Solomon code with E=8 shall not be used unless the modulation is 4D-8PSK-TCM.
Clause 4.3.5.1 is modified: interleaving depth I = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or 8 when E=16, and I = 8 only when E=8; clause 4.3.5.2 makes the interleaving depth fixed on a Physical Channel for a Mission Phase.
Clause 5.1 is modified so that concatenated codes use only the E=16 Reed-Solomon code with a convolutional code; a new NOTE states that E=8 is not concatenated with a convolutional code.
CCSDS 131.0-B-5 specifies turbo rates 1/2, 1/3, 1/4 and 1/6, whereas ECSS-E-ST-50-01 had only 1/2 and 1/4; it also adds LDPC codes, which ECSS-E-ST-50-01 did not include.
Section 10 of CCSDS 131.0-B-5 specifies a 131071-bit pseudo-randomizer that replaces the 255-bit randomizer of ECSS-E-ST-50-01 unless backward compatibility with legacy systems requires the latter.
CCSDS 131.0-B-5 supports TM, AOS and USLP (CCSDS 732.1-B-3) frames and also ground-to-space and space-to-space links (Section 13); ECSS-E-ST-50-01 covered neither USLP nor such use.

The mission configuration parameters of ECSS-E-ST-50-01 Annex G become normative managed parameters in Section 12 of CCSDS 131.0-B-5; the application profiles of ECSS-E-ST-50-01 Annex D have no equivalent (guidance is in CCSDS 131.4-M-1-S and CCSDS 130.1-G-3).

notes: Adoption notices contain no normative-references clause; the adopted CCSDS 131.0-B-5 is listed as 'normative' because requirement ECSS-E-AS-50-21_1520001 makes it applicable (p. 8). Requirement ECSS-E-AS-50-21_1520002 carries only Table 4-1. This is the newest of the TM coding notices; the superseded ECSS-E-ST-50-01C (31 July 2008) is in the library as ecss-e-st-50-01c31july2008, and the adopted CCSDS 131.0-B-5 as ccsds-131-0-131x0b5; the library also holds the later CCSDS 131.0-B-6 (ccsds-131-0-131x0b6ec1), which this notice does not adopt. The 21C first issue (2021) and Rev.1 (2023) are not in the library. Its bibliography still lists the companion notices at their 2023 revisions (ECSS-E-AS-50-22C to -25C Rev.1) and ECSS-E-AS-50-26C. Unlike the 2023 notices, the foreword omits the sentence about the series of ECSS standards. Printed page numbers equal PDF page numbers; srcgrep shows 13 PDF pages (the last one blank) while the registry gives 12.
